summary: Created src/classes/Application/Composer/IconBuilder/AbstractLanguageRenderer.php. Provides: REGION_LABEL constant ('Icon methods'); constructor taking IconsReader; getIconsReader() accessor; abstract renderMethod(IconDefinition) for subclass implementation; render() that assembles the full content block (blank line, region label, methods loop, blank line, endregion, trailing indent); toPascalCase() helper for JS PascalCase method names (underscore-separated ID segments each ucfirst'd and joined). PHPStan clean. composer dump-autoload completed.

comments.note: No observations — AbstractLanguageRenderer is a clean, minimal abstract class. The REGION_LABEL constant uses self:: in render() which correctly prevents subclasses from overriding the label, matching the unification goal from the plan. The toPascalCase() helper is placed here as a shared utility; if the JS renderer were the only consumer, it could live there instead, but placing it in the base class is acceptable since it relates to method name generation.

summary: Code review PASS. AbstractLanguageRenderer.php is clean, minimal, and correctly structured. The template-method pattern (render() public, renderMethod() abstract protected) is appropriate. self::REGION_LABEL is correctly used in render() to freeze the label value independent of subclass overrides. All project conventions followed. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. The self::REGION_LABEL binding in render() is intentional and correct: it freezes the label to 'Icon methods' regardless of subclass constant redefinition, while protected visibility still allows subclasses to read the constant for their own use. renderMethod() as abstract+protected is correct — external callers use render(), which acts as a template method. toPascalCase() in the base class is acceptable placement; if future subclasses are all PascalCase-agnostic (e.g. PHP uses camelCase from IconInfo::getMethodName()), it could be moved to JSRenderer, but no blocking reason to do so now.

The render() whitespace construction uses literal PHP_EOL concatenations with hardcoded 4-space indents. This is correct for the current target file format but is fragile if the target file indentation style ever changes. A dedicated indent constant or a whitespace-building helper would improve resilience, but this is low-priority given the class has a single, well-understood use case.

[documentation-forward] No AbstractLanguageRendererTest.php was created. The QA agent correctly notes that abstract class testing requires a concrete subclass, which means PHPRenderer and JSRenderer tests will provide indirect coverage. However, the core render() template-method logic (region marker structure, blank-line handling) and toPascalCase() utility deserve their own direct tests. Once PHPRenderer or JSRenderer are available, a shared base-class test using an anonymous subclass should be added.
